assertions.description: The position-visibility property itself is recognised — its initial value `always` parses. Without the property, none of the values below can be evaluated.
`position-visibility: anchor-valid` is accepted. This is the renamed singular value that replaced the reverted `anchors-valid`.
Setting `position-visibility: anchor-valid` on an element retains the declaration — the parser keeps it rather than dropping it, which is the stronger check that CSS.supports() alone does not make.
The two conditions compose: `position-visibility: anchor-valid anchor-visible` is a valid declaration, hiding the element when either condition is met.

`position-anchor` is supported. The resolved semantics of anchor-valid consider only the DEFAULT anchor, which is the one position-anchor names — so the property is a direct prerequisite for the value's definition, not an unrelated baseline check.

An element with `position-visibility: anchor-valid` becomes hidden (strongly hidden, skipping painting and hit-testing) once its default anchor stops being an acceptable anchor element — removed from the DOM, not rendered, or otherwise unacceptable. Losing a non-default anchor referenced only by anchor() must NOT hide it.
assertions.test: Requires a browser implementing the value. Observe in v157/css-position-visibility-anchor-s-valid/default-anchor-semantics/: remove the default anchor and confirm the card hides; remove a secondary anchor and confirm it does not.
